4
The diagram shows two fixed pins, Y and Z. A length of elastic is stretched between Y and Z and
around pin X, which is attached to a trolley.
Y
50 mm
80 mm
X
P
trolley
Z
30 mm
X is at the centre of the elastic and the trolley is to be propelled in the direction P at right angles
to YZ. The tension in the elastic is 4.0 N.
What is the force accelerating the trolley in the direction P when the trolley is released?
A
2.4 N
B
3.2 N
C
4.8 N
D 6.4 N

hints: Notice the right-angled triangle at X: $30 \text{ mm}$ sideways from YZ and $40 \text{ mm}$ half of the $80 \text{ mm}$ YZ length, with $50 \text{ mm}$ elastic length.
Each half of the elastic pulls pin X toward Y and toward Z with tension $4.0 \text{ N}$, so resolve each $4.0 \text{ N}$ force into a component along P and a component along YZ.
Only the components pointing toward YZ add in direction P, each equal to $4.0 \text{ N}$ times $30/50$. Add the two sides and check the perpendicular components cancel.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: P is at right angles to YZ, X is $30 \text{ mm}$ from the YZ line, and half of YZ is $80/2 = 40 \text{ mm}$. This gives a $30$-$40$-$50$ triangle with hypotenuse $50 \text{ mm}$ along each half of the elastic.
State the rule: the resultant force in direction P is the sum of the P-components of the two tension forces on pin X. Components perpendicular to P cancel by symmetry.
For the XY section, the cosine of the angle between XY and direction P is adjacent over hypotenuse $= 30/50 = 0.60$. So P-component from XY is $F_1 = 4.0 \times 0.60 = 2.4 \text{ N}$.
The XZ section is symmetric, so its P-component is also $F_2 = 4.0 \times 0.60 = 2.4 \text{ N}$, while its $40/50$ component along YZ is opposite to that from XY.
Add the P-components: $F = 2.4 + 2.4 = 4.8 \text{ N}$ toward P. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $4.0 \times 30/50 = 2.4 \text{ N}$, the P-component from only one side of the elastic. Both XY and XZ pull on X.

B.explanation: This is $2 \times 4.0 \times 40/50 = 3.2 \text{ N}$, using the component parallel to YZ. Those two components are opposite and cancel.

C.explanation: Both $4.0 \text{ N}$ tensions have P-component $4.0 \times 30/50$, giving $2 \times 2.4 = 4.8 \text{ N}$ in direction P.

D.explanation: This is $2 \times 4.0 \times 40/50 = 6.4 \text{ N}$, the sum of the magnitudes of the components parallel to YZ, which act in opposite directions.
